$description: WordPress editorial type styles (Figma Editorial/... in the main file; WordPress only). Families reference font.theme.* (tokens/wordpress/type-theme/), so they follow the theme. Line height is a ratio (px in lineHeightPx); letter spacing is em (Figma px and % in $extensions). Generated by scripts/build-tokens/make-tokens.py; never edit by hand.

default.$description: Article body copy. Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.

excerpt.$description: Card excerpt (dek), default. Production .archive-view .excerpt: 15px / 1.4 = 21px. Used by the Photos lead (feature-media) and regular section cards (feature-medium). Confirmed live 2026-10-02, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord and mcall; does not change with screen width.

excerpt-compact.$description: Card excerpt (dek), compact. Production 15px / 1.26667 = 19px on .feature-primary .feature-large (Top Zone lead), .feature-section .feature-large (section-block lead) and the 3/4-up .section-highlight lead cards. Family is body-family, except the section-highlight lead cards, which take font/theme/small-headline-family in production. Confirmed live 2026-10-02 on the same 6 sites; does not change with screen width.

copyright.$description: Measured live 2026-09-10 at 12.48px on all 6 repertoire sites — aliased to the existing font/size/12 primitive (same rounding treatment as font/size/14 @ ~14.06px measured and font/size/19 @ ~19.2px measured).

com.mng.note: No line height or letter spacing in Figma yet, so not a typography composite.

module-header.$description: 20px — confirmed live 2026-09-10 on all 6 repertoire sites, on the visible module-header element. Note: each site also carries a 30px/600 h2 with this same font/family styling, but it is a screen-reader-only (visually hidden) accessibility label, not a rendered design element — deliberately not tokenized here. See font-token-audit.md for detail.

com.mng.note: No line height or letter spacing in Figma yet, so not a typography composite.

primary-label.$description: 15px — confirmed live 2026-09-10 on all 6 repertoire sites.

com.mng.note: No line height or letter spacing in Figma yet, so not a typography composite.

card-quaternary.$description: Fourth-tier card headline (Section Highlight, feature-medium + feature-large). Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.

card-secondary.$description: Second-tier homepage card headline (Section Highlight, feature-medium). Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.

card-tertiary.$description: Third-tier card headline (top-of-page block, feature-small). Not the module header (20/600). Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.

card-tertiary-compact.$description: TOP ZONE small card headline at 800–1039px (production .feature-primary article.feature-small, vertical card with a 16:9 image on top). Noto heading family 700, 16px / 18.88px (×1.18), no letter spacing. Confirmed live 2026-10-07 at 1024px, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, mcall and canoncitydailyrecord. At 1280 production uses CardTertiary (vertical 340px card, 16:9 image).

card-tertiary-row.$description: TOP ZONE small card headline at the 1100px template (≥1040px, below the 1280 layout) (production .feature-primary article.feature-small, horizontal card with a 280×157 image on the left). Noto heading family 700, 18px / 21.6px (×1.2), no letter spacing. Confirmed live 2026-10-07 at 1100px, identical on the same 6 sites. At 1280 production uses CardTertiary (vertical 340px card, 16:9 image).

display.$description: Corrected 2026-08-27 to the confirmed live article H1 size (36px). Previously aliased to Font Size 9 (29px), which is actually the lead-card size (see Titles/Title).

headline-list.$description: Headline-only list items in Section Highlight; the most common headline on every homepage. Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.

related-headline.$description: "More News" headlines on article pages. Letter spacing is normal (0). Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.

section-header.$description: Section-front page H1 (e.g. a category landing page's "Sports" heading). Confirmed live 2026-09-10 on ocregister.com/sports/ and chicagotribune.com/sports/ (className "section-header"). Consolidates CRUX Style Library's sectionH1 and mastheadSectionH1 tokens, which were identical duplicates (both 40/700). Aliased to font/theme/heading-family since production renders it in the theme's heading font.

com.mng.note: No line height or letter spacing in Figma yet, so not a typography composite.

subtitle.$description: Corrected 2026-08-27 to the confirmed live article deck/subhead size (23px). Previously aliased to Font Size 9 (29px), which is actually the lead-card size (see Titles/Title) — Subtitle was indistinguishable from Title/Display before this fix.

title.$description: Confirmed live 2026-08-27: headline family for the Measured Vibrant/Bold Coastal theme cluster. Modern Earthy/Morning Call use Noto Sans instead — this composite is not yet theme-aware (single mode); promoting it into a themed collection is a follow-up. Updated 2026-09-09: now aliased to font/theme/heading-family instead of a hard-coded "Noto Serif" literal, so this composite correctly follows the Modern Earthy / Morning Call reversal (heading=Noto Sans there).

title-media.$description: Lead-story headline in the homepage media block (feature-large in feature-media). Sibling of Editorial/Titles/Title. Confirmed live 2026-09-24, identical on ocregister, denverpost, chicagotribune, orlandosentinel, canoncitydailyrecord, mcall and greeleytribune.
